title: SDK Contract Testing and Sample Workflows
author: Aria Patel
body:
Overview

This document defines recommended patterns for SDK contract tests, CI workflows, and sample test suites for Redwood Inference SDKs. It is intended for SDK authors, integration engineers, and platform CI owners. The goal is to ensure language bindings and client libraries remain compatible with the Redwood API surface across releases, and to provide reproducible templates engineers can copy into projects.

When to use SDK contract tests

- Before any public SDK release or patch that changes request/response shapes.
- Prior to rolling a runtime/major API change (model routing, function calling schema changes).
- In nightly CI runs for long-lived SDK repositories.

Test types and scope

1) Contract unit tests (fast, deterministic)
   - Validate request builders encode parameters into the expected HTTP payloads.
   - Validate response parsers tolerate optional/missing fields.
   - Run with stubbed HTTP server or request fixtures.

2) Integration contract tests (CI gated)
   - Hit a sandbox Redwood API or test harness endpoint.
   - Exercise end-to-end serialization, headers, auth refresh, streaming and chunked responses.

3) Regression scenario tests
   - Use small prompt sets and expected token patterns to detect behavior regressions (not full evals).

Ownership and SLOs

- SDK Team (owner): maintains test suites and CI pipelines.
- DevEx Platform (support): provides the sandbox endpoint, test tokens, and reusable GitHub Actions templates.
- SLO: tests must complete within CI max time of 15 minutes on PRs, nightly runs may take up to 1 hour.

Contract schema (recommended minimal surface)

Use a small, explicit contract YAML that lives in repo root as tests/contract.yaml. This file is the canonical expected shape used by unit and integration tests. Example: 

```yaml
api_contract_version: 1
endpoints:
  - name: text_generate
    method: POST
    path: /v1/generate
    required_request_fields:
      - model
      - input
    optional_request_fields:
      - max_tokens
      - temperature
    response_expectations:
      - field: output.choices
        type: list
      - field: output.truncated
        type: boolean

  - name: embeddings
    method: POST
    path: /v1/embeddings
    required_request_fields:
      - model
      - input
    response_expectations:
      - field: embeddings
        type: list
        item_type: float
```

Sample workflows

A. PR fast-path: unit contract tests only (recommended for contributor experience)

1. On PR: run lint, unit contract tests, and small type checks.
2. If unit contract tests pass, allow merge to main with maintainer approval.
3. On merge: trigger full integration pipeline (see B).

B. Merge gate: full integration + nightly regression

1. On push to main: build SDK artifacts, run integration contract tests against sandbox.
2. If integration tests fail, automatically open an issue with artifacts and last failing request/response.
3. Nightly: run extended regression suite across language matrix (see matrix below).

CI template (GitHub Actions example)

```yaml
name: SDK Contract CI
on: [pull_request, push]
jobs:
  contract_unit:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - name: Setup runtime
        run: ./ci/setup-env.sh
      - name: Install dependencies
        run: ci/install_deps.sh
      - name: Run contract unit tests
        run: ci/run_contract_unit_tests.sh
  integration_tests:
    needs: contract_unit
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    if: github.event_name == 'push' || github.event.pull_request.merged == true
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - name: Setup sandbox creds
        run: echo "REDWOOD_TEST_TOKEN=${{ secrets.REDWOOD_TEST_TOKEN }}" >> $GITHUB_ENV
      - name: Run integration contract tests
        env:
          REDWOOD_TEST_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.REDWOOD_TEST_TOKEN }}
        run: ci/run_integration_tests.sh
```

Testing matrix (example)

| SDK language | Unit coverage | Integration frequency | Responsible owner |
|-------------|---------------|-----------------------|--------------------|
| python      | 95% unit     | nightly + on-merge   | aria-patel         |
| javascript  | 90% unit     | nightly + on-merge   | samir-desai        |
| go          | 85% unit     | nightly              | lina-cho           |
| dotnet      | 80% unit     | weekly               | contract-maintain  |

Implementation patterns and helpers

- Use a lightweight contract validator library (recommendation: internal package devx-contracts v0.x).
- Store request/response fixtures under tests/fixtures/{unit,integration}. Keep fixtures < 200KB.
- For unit tests, prefer a local mock server (python: responses, node: nock, go: httptest).
- For integration tests, use the sandbox host: https://sandbox-inference.redwood.company (token provided via secrets).

Common failure modes and canonical fixes

1) Failure: Parsers crash when optional fields missing
   - Symptom: stack trace referencing KeyError/TypeError in response deserializer.
   - Fix: Update parser to use safe accessors and provide defaults. Add unit test using fixture that omits optional fields.

2) Failure: Streaming tests hang in CI
   - Symptom: GH Action job times out at 15m during streaming scenario.
   - Fix: Ensure test harness enforces a shorter read timeout (suggest 30s) and that CI container has correct netcat/tcpreplay configs. Add a watchdog in test that cancels read after N tokens.

3) Failure: Authentication flakes in integration runs
   - Symptom: 401 returned intermittently, usually on long-running jobs.
   - Fix: Use short-lived test tokens refreshed by runtime or switch to token rotation helper in ci/setup-env.sh. Add telemetry to record token expiry.

4) Failure: Contract drift after runtime change
   - Symptom: many SDK tests failing with mismatched field names.
   - Fix: Coordinate with runtime release owner to publish contract_delta.md. For urgent rollbacks, pin SDK CI to prior API contract by using ci/contract_mocks.yaml for temporary compatibility.

Publisher checklist (pre-release)

- [ ] Update tests/contract.yaml if API surface changed.
- [ ] Run full integration suite locally against sandbox.
- [ ] Bump SDK version, update CHANGELOG with contract notes.
- [ ] Tag a release and confirm CI publishes artifacts to internal registry.

Troubleshooting commands and snippets

- Run unit contract tests locally:
  - Linux/macOS: ./ci/run_contract_unit_tests.sh --fast

- Replay a failing request against sandbox:

```bash
# echo saved request to file request.json then
curl -X POST \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_TEST_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  https://sandbox-inference.redwood.company/v1/generate \
  --data-binary @request.json
```

- Generate a diagnostic bundle to attach to issues:

```bash
ci/collect_diagnostics.sh --output /tmp/sdk-diag.tar.gz
```

Appendix: small checklist for SDK authors

- Keep fixtures small and descriptive.
- Add a human-readable contract change note in the pull request description when you modify contract.yaml.
- When debugging flakey tests, run in a clean container to reproduce network/time-sensitive issues.
